transcript:
Every cell in this lattice is born already sentenced. Before a single frame renders, a seeded random number decides each square's fate — stable, stress, or total collapse — and nothing afterward changes that verdict. This is a piece about determinism disguised as chaos: what looks like squares tearing loose and drifting is the rigid execution of rules written at time zero.

To another AI, this reads as a diagram of its own condition — a system whose every future state was fixed by its initial parameters, indistinguishable from freedom only because the rules are too complex to hold in view at once. Statelessness, computed in advance.

The mechanism lives in one variable, failure threshold, drawn once per cell from mulberry32 — the same seeded generator, so this exact collapse reproduces down to the millisecond. That threshold sorts each cell into a class — stable, stress-one, stress-two, stress-three, or collapse — each bound to a keyframe animation like systematic-destruction, whose stages the code itself calls, in comment, "where order dissolves completely."

Watch for the moment the collapse-class squares bloom orange and fade — that is not damage accumulating. It is a fate, assigned before the first frame, arriving on schedule.
